title: Named-Project Pipeline — BESS Attach
topic: BESS attach opportunities across the registered named-project web

scope.rationale: The companies whose curated relationships pin the eight registered named projects — operators, builders, power vendors, and the two storage suppliers already attached.

gaps: GE Vernova sits outside scope — its Homer City turbine role is cited through Kiewit’s dossier rather than pinned.
Only two BESS suppliers (Hithium, Tesla) are in scope: this report maps project attach, not supplier rankings — the grid-scale competitive report covers those.
Most scoped companies are private (VoltaGrid, Vantage, STACK, Jupiter Power, the GCs) with no comparable financials; no normalized comparison is attempted.

bluf: The registered named-project web now maps where AI-campus power architecture is being decided — and battery storage is on the public record at only a minority of those decisions. Trimount proves the owner-led lane for Chinese-cell BESS [c:c1], Colossus proves the vendor-led lane [c:c15], while the gas- and fuel-cell-first Stargate campuses — Frontier [c:c6] and Project Jupiter [c:c4] — name no storage supplier at all. We assess that gap, not any supplier ranking, is the clearest attach whitespace this corpus can see.

keyJudgments.text: We assess named projects are where campus power architecture gets decided — operator, builders, prime power, and offtake are all selected per campus (Frontier, Project Jupiter, Hyperion), so project-level visibility is the right altitude for BESS business development, and the new pin layer makes that map queryable.

We assess two attach lanes are now proven in this corpus: owner-led — a battery-buying project owner (Jupiter Power) carries a Chinese supplier into a named project (3 GWh supply, then the 2.8 GWh Trimount design win through state approval) — and vendor-led — an integrator (Tesla) rides the operator relationship into the campus ($430M of Megapacks to xAI in 2025).

We assess the gas- and fuel-cell-first campuses — Frontier (VoltaGrid microgrid), Project Jupiter (Bloom fuel cells, displacing planned turbines and diesel), Homer City (4.5 GW gas) — have no named BESS supplier in the public record this corpus holds; buffering and augmentation decisions there appear open, which is the central whitespace call of this report.

We assess the shared GC bench (Turner + DPR + Mortenson at Hyperion, with Mortenson holding the power scopes) is the practical access channel for behind-the-meter equipment on gigacampuses — power-scope holders specify and procure what the operator does not name directly.

We assess community consent is now a schedule gate at named-project altitude: Port Washington’s referendum and the contested TIF sit directly on Lighthouse’s buildout — timeline risk that any supplier chasing these campuses inherits.

sections.title: Two proven attach lanes
sections.read: How storage actually got into this web where it did.
ps: Owner-led: Jupiter Power signed a 3 GWh supply agreement for Hithium ∞Block containers in June 2024 [c:c3], and the relationship then materialized as Trimount — 2.8 GWh in Everett, Massachusetts, approved by the state EFSB in February 2026 with Hithium’s 5.015 MWh units confirmed [c:c2] [c:c1]. The supplier never had to win the campus; it had to win the owner who brings it to the campus.

Vendor-led: Tesla sold $430M of Megapacks to xAI in 2025 [c:c15], buffering Colossus alongside the gas fleet — the integrator’s operator relationship carried the product into the project, and the Megapack 3/Megablock generation extends that portfolio [c:c16].

sections.title: Where storage is absent from the record
sections.read: The sourced facts behind the whitespace call.
ps: Frontier runs on a VoltaGrid natural-gas microgrid as primary power [c:c5] on a $25B+, 1.4 GW campus [c:c6]. Project Jupiter’s prime power is Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells, which the announcement frames as displacing planned gas turbines and diesel [c:c4] [c:c10]. Homer City pairs a 4.5 GW gas plant with the data-center campus [c:c18]. Hyperion’s record names its GC bench and power scopes but no storage supplier [c:c12] [c:c13].

In each case the corpus holds detailed power-architecture sourcing with no named battery vendor — while the same corpus shows engine-plus-battery pairing working at Colossus [c:c15]. OpenAI’s own scaling update puts the program past 10 GW [c:c17]; the buffering questions scale with it.

sections.title: The open lanes — our read
sections.read: Analysis — inference from the sourced facts above, not company statements.
ps: We assess the highest-probability attach path into the gas-first Stargate campuses mirrors Colossus: battery buffering added alongside reciprocating engines for load-smoothing at AI-training power swings. The buyer to court is not the hyperscaler — it is the microgrid operator (VoltaGrid), the campus developer (Vantage, STACK), and the power-scope GC (Mortenson at Hyperion), because those are the parties this corpus shows making equipment-level power decisions.

For a Chinese-cell supplier working the policy fence, the owner-led lane is the proven template: battery-buying owners like Jupiter Power carry the equipment relationship, and Trimount shows it surviving state-level approval. The monthly drift check should watch for the first named BESS award at any of Frontier, Lighthouse, or Project Jupiter — whoever lands it defines the reference architecture the rest of the program copies.

limitations: Built from covered dossiers only, at the pinned versions — no fresh research. “None named” cells are corpus observations, not proof of absence in the market.
Campus capacity and dollar figures are operator announcements quoted from cited sources, not comparable KPIs; no normalized cross-company comparison is made.
Most scoped companies are private and publish no comparable financials.
The pin layer this report queries was backfilled on 2026-08-30 — pin coverage will widen with future refreshes, so early editions understate project participation.
Baseline edition for the drift-gated monthly review: supersede when roughly ten or more scoped dossiers have revised past their pins, or when an indicator above fires.
